questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{2y}, y\left(0\right) = 1,$~then $y ( 1 )$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{2}^{x + y} - {2}^{x}}{2y} = {2}^{x} \left(\dfrac{{2}^{y} - 1}{2y}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2y}{{2}^{y} - 1})$dy = {2}^{x}dx$

By using Variable Separable method

$∫ $\dfrac{{2}^{y}dy}{{2}^{y} - 1} =$∫ {2}^{x}dx$

Let ${2}^{y} - 1 = t ⇒ {2}^{y}\ln \left(2\right)dy = dt$

$∫ $\dfrac{dt}{t}\dfrac{1}{ℓn2} =$∫ {2}^{x}dx$

We know that~$∫ $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx = \ln \left(x\right) + c \text{ and } ∫ a^{x}dx = $\dfrac{ax}{\ln \left(a\right)} +$c .$

$⇒ $\dfrac{\ln \left(t\right)}{\ln \left(2\right)} = \dfrac{2x}{\ln \left(2\right)} + \dfrac{c}{\ln \left(2\right)}

$⇒ \ln \left(t\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

$⇒ \ln \left({2}^{y} -1\right) = {2}^{x} + c$

when $x = 0, y = 1 ⇒ \ln \left(2 - 1\right) = {2}^{0} + c$

$⇒ c = - 1 .$

$⇒ \ln \left({2}^{y} -1\right) = {2}^{x} - 1$

$⇒ {2}^{y} - 1 = e^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

$⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + e^{{2}^{x} - 1}$

when $x = 1 ⇒ {2}^{y} = 1 + e^{1} ⇒ y = \log_{2} ( 1 + e )$

$

questions.q: If the solution curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$~of the differential equation $y^{2}dx +  \left(x^{2} - xy + y^{2}\right)dy = 0$, which passes through the point~\left(1, 1\right)$ and intersects the line $y = \sqrt{3}x$~at the point  \left(\alpha, \sqrt{3}\alpha\right),then value of $\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\sqrt{3}\alpha\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $y^{2}dx + \left(x^{2} - xy + y^{2}\right)dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = - \left(x^{2} - xy + y^{2}\right)y^{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now let $x = vy⇒ v + $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = \dfrac{dx}{dy}

Now putting in equation \left(i\right)$ we get

$⇒ v + $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = - \left(v^{2} - v + 1\right)$

$⇒ $y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = -$v^{2} - 1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- dv}{1 + v^{2}} = \dfrac{dy}{y}~

Now Integrating Both side

$⇒ - ∫ $\dfrac{dy}{1 + v^{2}} =$∫ $\dfrac{dy}{y}

$⇒ - \tan^{- 1}v = \log \left|y\right| + c$~$⇒ - \tan^{- 1} $\left(\dfrac{x}{y}) =$\log \left|$y\right| + c$

Also~ this curve passes through \left($1, 1\right)$~

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}1 = $\log \left|$1\right| + c$~$⇒ c = - $\dfrac{π}{4}

$⇒ - \tan^{- $1}\dfrac{x}{y} = $\log \left|$y\right| - $\dfrac{π}{4}

Now putting $y = $\sqrt{3}$x$~and $x = $\alpha~we get

$= - \tan^{- 1}$\ddfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}x} =$\log \left|$\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| - \dfrac{π}{4}$~$= - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{3} = $\log \left(\sqrt{3}\alpha) - \dfrac{π}{4}$

$= - \dfrac{π}{6} + \dfrac{π}{4} =$\log \left|$\sqrt{3}\alpha\right|$

$⇒ $\log \left|$\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| = \dfrac{π}{12}$

questions.q: If $y = y ( x )$ is the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = ( \tan x - y ) \sec^{2}x$ , $x \in \left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) , such that $y  \left(0\right) = 0$, then $y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given differential equation can be written as
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\sec^{2}x = \tan x . \sec^{2}x$
Integrating factor $= e^{∫ \sec^{2}xdx} = e^{\tan x}$
Hence, solution of given differential equation,
$y . e^{\tan x} = ∫ \tan x . \sec^{2}x . e^{\tan x}dx$
$⇒ y . e^{\tan x} = \tan x . e^{\tan x} - ∫ sec^{2}x . e^{\tan x}dx$~ ~(using integration by parts)

$⇒ y . e^{\tan x} = \tan x . e^{\tan x} - e^{\tan x} + c$

Given,~$y\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 1$

Solution of given differential is

$y . e^{\tan x} = \tan x . e^{\tan x} - e^{\tan x} + 1$

Hence,~$y\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\left(- 1\right)e^{- 1} - e^{- 1} + 1}{e- 1}$

~$⇒ y\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = e - 2$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be a solution curve of the differential equation,~  \left(1 - x^{2}y^{2}\right)dx = ydx + xdy$, If the line $x = 1$~intersects the curve $y = y\left(x\right)$ at $y = 2$~and the line $x = 2$~intersects the curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$ at $y = \alpha,$then a value of $\alpha$is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(1 - x^{2}y^{2}\right)dx = ydx + xdy$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{ydx + xdy}{1 - \left(xy\right)2}$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{d\left(yx\right)}{1 - \left(xy\right)2}$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{d \left(xy\right)}{1 - xy} + \dfrac{d\left(xy\right)}{1 + xy}\right)

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ 2x + c = $\ln \left|\dfrac{1 + xy}{1 - xy}\right|

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{xy + 1}{xy - 1}\right| =$e^{c}e^{2x}$

Now given,~y\left($1\right) = 2$~so putting the value in above equation we get,

$3 = e^{c}e^{2}$

$⇒ e^{c} = $\dfrac{3}{e2}

Hence, the equation becomes~ \left|$\dfrac{xy + 1}{xy - 1}\right| =3e^{2x - 2}$

Now finding y\left($2\right)$~so putting $x = 2$~in above equation we get,~

\left|$\dfrac{2y + 1}{2y - 1}\right| =3e^{2}$

$⇒ 2y + 1 = 2 \cdot3e^{2}y - 3e^{2}$

$⇒ 1 + 3e^{2} = 2y \left($3e^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ $y\left($2\right) = \dfrac{1 + 3e^{2}}{2\left(3e^{2} - 1\right)}$

questions.q: & If& $x^{3}dy + xy \cdot dx = x^{2}dy + 2ydx; y  \left(2\right) = e$ and $x > 1$, then $y\left(4\right) is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $x^{3}dy + xy \cdot dx = x^{2}dy + 2ydx$

$⇒ \left(x^{3} - x^{2}\right)dy = \left(2 - x\right)ydx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} = \left(2 - x\right)\left(x^{3} - x^{2}\right)dx$

Integrating both sides with respect to~$x$, we get

$∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} = ∫ \left(2 - x\right)x^{2} \left($x - 1\right)dx + k . . . . . . . . . . . . \left($i\right)$

Let~ \left(2 - x\right)x^{2} \left(x - 1\right) = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{x2} +C\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(2 - x\right) = Ax\left(x - 1\right) + B\left(x - 1\right) + Cx^{2}$

Putting~$x = 0 ⇒ 2 = - B ⇒ B = - 2$

Putting~$x = 1 ⇒ 2 - 1 = C ⇒ C = 1$

Putting~$x = 2 ⇒ 2 - 2 = A\left(2\right)\left(1\right) + B \left($1\right) + C \left({2}^{2}\right)⇒ 2A + 2 = 0 ⇒ A = - 1$

From equation~ \left($i\right)$, we get

$∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} =∫ \left(\dfrac{- 1}{x} + \dfrac{- 2}{x2} + \dfrac{1}{x - 1}\right)$dx + k$

$⇒ \ln y = - \ln x + $\dfrac{2}{x} +$\ln \left|$x - 1\right| + k . . . . . . . . . . \left($ii\right)$

Given~y\left($2\right) = e$~i.e. at~$x = 2, y = e$

$⇒ lne = - \ln 2 + $\dfrac{2}{2} +\ln \left|$2 - 1\right| + k$

$⇒ 1 = - \ln 2 + 1 + 0 + k$

$⇒ k = \ln 2$

Putting in equation~ \left($ii\right)$, we get

$\ln y = - \ln x + \dfrac{2}{x} ++$\ln \left|x - 1\right| + \ln 2$

Now putting~$x = 4$, we get

$\ln y = - \ln 4 + $\dfrac{2}{4} ++$\ln \left|$4 - 1\right| + \ln 2$

$⇒ \ln y = - 2\ln 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} +\ln 3 + \ln 2$

$⇒ \ln y = - \ln 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} +\ln 3$

$⇒ \ln y = \dfrac{1}{2} +$++ln\dfrac{3}{2}

$⇒ $ln\dfrac{2y}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{2y}{3} =$==e\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{e}$

$⇒ $y\left($4\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{e}$

$

questions.q: Let $f(x)=x-1$ and $g(x)=e^x$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$. If $\frac{d y}{d x}=\left(e^{-2 \sqrt{x}} g(f(f(x)))-\frac{y}{\sqrt{x}}\right), y(0)=0$, then $y(1)$ is :-
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=x-1 \\ & f(f(x))=f(x)-1=x-1-1=x-2 \\ & g(f(f(x)))=e^{x-2} \\ & \therefore \frac{d y}{d x}=e^{-2 \sqrt{x}} \times e^{x-2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} y \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} y=e^{x-2 \sqrt{x}-2} \text { which is L.D.E } \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{d y}{\sqrt{x}}}=e^{2 \sqrt{x}}
\end{aligned}$
Its solution is
$\begin{aligned}
& y \times e^{2 \sqrt{x}}=\int e^{2 \sqrt{x}} \times e^{x-2 \sqrt{x}-2} d x+c \\ & y \times e^{2 \sqrt{x}}=\int e^{x-2} d x+c \\ & y \times e^{2 \sqrt{x}}=e^{x-2}+c
\end{aligned}$
$\text { Given } \mathrm{x}=0, \mathrm{y}=0 \Rightarrow 0=\mathrme^{-2}+\mathrm{c} \quad ; \mathrm{c}=-\mathrme^{-2}$
$\therefore \mathrm{y} \times \mathrme^{2 \sqrt{\mathrm{x}}}=\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}-2}-\mathrme^{-2}$
$\text { when } \mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{y} \times \mathrm{e}^2=\mathrme^{-1}-\mathrme^{-2}$
$y=\frac{e^{-1}-e^{-2}}{e^2}=\frac{\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{e^2}}{e^2}=\frac{e^2-e}{e^5}=\frac{e-1}{e^4}$
Option (1) is correct

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(3y^{2} - 5x^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)dy = 0$ such that $y ( 1 ) = 1$. Then \left|( y ( 2 ) {)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right|$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

\left(3y^{2} - 5x^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y\left(5x^{2} - 3y^{2}\right)}{2x\left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)}$

This is homogeneous differential equation

Let~$y = tx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{( tx ) \left(5x^{2} - 3t^{2}x^{2}\right)}{2x\left(x^{2} - t^{2}x^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{t\left(5 - 3t^{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - t^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{5t - 3t^{3}}{2 - 2t^{2}} - t = \dfrac{3t - t^{3}}{2 - 2t^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(1 - t^{2}\right)}{3t - t^{3}}dt = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

Taking integration on both sides we get,

$∫ \dfrac{2 \left(1 - t^{2}\right)}{3t - t^{3}}dt = ∫ $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let~$3t - t^{3} = z ⇒ 3\left(1 - t^{2}\right)dt = dz$

$⇒ \left(1 - t^{2}\right)dt = \dfrac{1}{3}dz$

Substitute in equation \left(1\right)$~we get,

$\dfrac{2}{3}∫ \dfrac{dz}{z} =∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}\ln ( z ) = \ln x + lnc$

$⇒ z\dfrac{2}{3} =cx ⇒ z = $c\$ddfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}

$⇒ 3t - t^{3} = $c\$ddfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}

Now put~$t = $\dfrac{y}{x}

$⇒ $\dfrac{3y}{x} - \dfrac{y3}{x3} =c\$ddfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}

Given~$y ( 1 ) = 1$~when~$x = 1, y = 1$

~$⇒ $c\dfrac{3}{2} =$2$

So, equation becomes~3\dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{y3}{x3} ==2x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3x^{2}y - y^{3} = 2x\dfrac{9}{2} . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Put~$x = 2$~in equation \left($2\right)$,

$12y ( 2 ) - \left($y ( 2 )\right)3 = 2 ( 2) \dfrac{9}{2} ===32\sqrt{2}$

$∴ \left|\left(y ( 2 )\right)3 - 12y ( 2 )\right| = 32\sqrt{2}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\tan x \cos x - 2\tan x \cdot y$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(2\tan x\right)y = 2\sin x$

Now solving linear differential equation by finding Integrating factor~$= e^{∫ 2tanxdx} = \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x}$

Solution is given by,

$y\left(\dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x}\right) = ∫ \dfrac{2\sin x}{\cos^{2}x}dx$

$⇒ y\sec^{2}x = \dfrac{2}{\cos x} + C$

$⇒ y = 2\cos x + C\cos^{2}x$

Passes through~ \left(\dfrac{π}{4}, 0\right)$

$⇒ 0 = \sqrt{2} + \dfrac{C}{2} ⇒ C = - 2\sqrt{2}$

So,~$f\left(x\right) = 2\cos x - 2\sqrt{2}\cos^{2}x$: Required curve

Now,~${∫}_{0}^{\pi2}ydx = 2{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}cosxdx - 2\sqrt{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\cos^{2}xdx$

$= {2\sin x}_{0}^{\pi2} - 2\sqrt{2}{\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{4}}_{0}^{\pi2}$

$= 2 - \dfrac{π}{2}$

$

questions.solution:
Given differential equation can be written as:
$y^{2}dx - xydy = x^{3}dx$
$⇒ \left(ydx - xdy\right) = \dfrac{x3}{y}dx$
$⇒ \dfrac{ydx - xdy}{y^{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}^{3}dx$
$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}{{\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}^{3}} = ∫ dx$
$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}^{- 3 + 1}}{- 3 + 1} = x + c$

$⇒ y^{2} = - 2x^{3} - cx^{2}$

$⇒ y^{2} + 2x^{3} + cx^{2} = 0$

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the points  \left(0, 2\right)$ and  \left(0, - 2\right)$ is

questions.solution:
Given a circle passing through \left(0, - 2\right)$ and \left(0, 2\right)$, so its equation will be,

\left(x - {x}_{1}\right)\left(x - {x}_{2}\right) + \left(y - {y}_{1}\right)\left(y - {y}_{2}\right) + {λ}_{1}\left|$\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ {x}_{1} & {y}_{1} & 1 \\ {x}_{2} & {y}_{2} & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0, \left({λ}_{1} \inR\right)

On putting the given values we get,

$⇒ \left($x - 0\right)\left(x - 0\right) + \left(y - 2\right)\left($y + 2\right) + {λ}_{1}\left|$\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0, \left({λ}_{1} \inR\right)

$⇒ x^{2} + \left($y^{2} - 4\right) + {λ}_{1} \left($4x\right) = 0$~

$⇒ x^{2} + \left($y^{2} - 4\right) + \lambdax = 0, \left(\lambda \in$R\right)$

Now dividing both side by $x$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{x^{2} + \left(y^{2} - 4\right)}{x} + \lambda =0$

Now differentiating with respect to $x$

$⇒ \dfrac{x\left[2x + 2y \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right] - \left[x^{2} + y^{2} - 4\right] \cdot 1}{x2} =0$

$⇒ 2xy $\cdot $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 4\right) = 0$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+x y=5 x^2 \sqrt{1+x^2} \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{x y}{1+x^2}=\frac{5 x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}} \\ & \therefore \text { I.F. }=\mathrme^{\int \frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+x^2} \mathrm{dx}}=\mathrme^{\frac{\ln \left(1+x^2\right)}{2}}=\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y} \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}=\int \frac{5 \mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}} \cdot \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y} \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}=\int \frac{5 \mathrm{x}^2}{\sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}} \cdot \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2} \mathrm{dx} \\ & \mathrm{y} \sqrt{1+\mathrm{x}^2}=\frac{5 \mathrm{x}^3}{3}+\mathrm{C} \\ & \because \mathrm{y}(0)=0 \Rightarrow 0=0+\mathrm{C} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=0\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \therefore y=\frac{5 x^3}{3 \sqrt{1+x^2}} \\ & y(\sqrt{3})=\frac{15 \sqrt{3}}{32}=\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$$

questions.q:
Which of the following is true for $y \left(x\right)$ that satisfies the differential equation

\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$xy - 1 + x - y; y\left(0\right) = 0

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(1 + y\right) \left($x - 1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{( y + 1 )} = \left($x - 1\right)dx$

Integrate both the sides we get,~

~\ln \left($y + 1\right) = $\dfrac{x2}{2} -$x + c$

Given~y\left($0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 0$

$∴ y = $e\left(\dfrac{x2}{2} -x) - 1

$

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation \left(x - y^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + y^{2}\right)dy = 0$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& \left(x - y^{2}\right)dx + y\left(5x + y^{2}\right)dy = 0$

After rearranging we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y^{2} - x}{y\left(5x + y^{2}\right)}$~

Now, let $y^{2} = v ⇒ 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\dfrac{1}{2y}\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v - x}{y \left($5x + v\right)}$

\dfrac{dv}{dx} =$2\left(\dfrac{v - x}{5x + v}\right)

Now let~$v = kx$

$⇒ k + x$\dfrac{dk}{dx} =$2 \left(\dfrac{kx - x}{5x + kx}\right)$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dk}{dx} = - \left(k^{2} + 3k + 2\right)k + 5$

$⇒ ∫ \left(5 + k\right)\left(k + 1\right)\left(k + 2\right)dk = ∫ - \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{4}{k + 1} - \dfrac{3}{k + 2}\right)dk = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ 4\ln \left(k + 1\right) - 3\ln \left(k + 2\right) = - \ln x + lnc$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(k + 1\right)4}{\left(k + 2\right)3} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 1\right)4}{\left(\dfrac{v}{x} + 2\right)3} = \dfrac{c}{x}$

$⇒ c\left(y^{2} + 2x\right)3 = \left(y^{2} + x\right)4$

$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right) be a differentiable function defined on  \left[0, 2\right]$ such that $f^{'} \left(x\right) = f^{'}  \left($2 - x\right)$ for all $x \in \left($0, 2\right), $f\left($0\right) = 1$ and f\left($2\right) = e^{2} .$~Then the value of ${∫}_{0}^{2}f\left($x\right)dx$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f^{'} \left(x\right) = f^{'} \left($2 - x\right)$

f\left($x\right) = - $f\left($2 - x\right) + c$

put~$x = 0$

f\left($0\right) = - $f\left($2\right) + c$

$c = $f\left($0\right) + $f\left($2\right) = 1 + e^{2}$

so,~f\left($x\right) + $f\left($2 - x\right) = 1 + e^{2}$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2}f\left($x\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2}f\left($2 - x\right)dx$

$2I = {∫}_{0}^{2}\lleft(f\left(x\right) + f\left(2 - x\right))dx$

$2I = \left(1 + e^{2}\right){∫}_{0}^{2}dx$

$I = 1 + e^{2}$

$

questions.q: Let $x = x  \left(y\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation 2ye\dfrac{x}{y2}$dx +  \left(y^{2} - 4xe\dfrac{x}{y2}\right)dy = 0$~such that x \left(1\right) = 0$. Then, $x\left(e\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$2ye\dfrac{x}{y2}dx + \left(y^{2} - 4xe\dfrac{x}{y2}\right)dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{y2}\left[ydx - 2xdy\right] + y^{2}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{y2}\left[\dfrac{y^{2}dx - x \cdot \left(2y\right)dy}{y}\right] + y^{2}dy = 0$

Divide by~$y^{3}$

$2e\dfrac{x}{y2}\left[\dfrac{y^{2}dx - x \cdot \left(2y\right)dy}{y4}\right] + \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{y2}d\left(\dfrac{x}{y2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

Now integrating both side we get,

$∫ 2e\dfrac{x}{y2}d\left(\dfrac{x}{y2}\right) + ∫ \dfrac{1}{y}dy = 0$

$2e\dfrac{x}{y2} + \ln y + c = 0$

Given,~ \left(0, 1\right)$~lies on it,~

So,~$2e^{0} + \ln 1 + c = 0 ⇒ c = - 2$~

Hence required curve:~$2e\dfrac{x}{y2} + \ln y - 2 = 0$

For~$x \left(e\right)$

2e\dfrac{x}{e2} +$lne - 2 = 0 ⇒ x = - e^{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2 \cos x \frac{\mathrm{~d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=\sin 2 x-4 y \sin x, x \in \left($0, $\frac{\pi}{2}\right). If $y  \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0$, then $y^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to $\qquad$ ________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}+2 y \tan x=\sin x \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{2 \int \tan x d x}=\sec ^2 x \\ & y \sec ^2 x=\int \frac{\sin x}{\cos ^2 x} d x \\ & =\int \tan x \sec x d x \\ & =\sec x+C \\ & C=-2\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & y=\cos x-2 \cos ^2 x \\ & y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-1 \\ & y^{\prime}=-\sin x+4 \cos x \sin x \\ & y^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+2 \\ & y^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $dy = e^{\alphax + y}dx; \alpha \inN .$If $y\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}2$~and $y\left(0\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right),$~then the value of \alpha is equal to ___.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $∫ e^{- y}dy = ∫ e^{\alphax}dx$

$⇒ - e^{- y} = \dfrac{e\alphax}{α} + c . . . \left(1\right)$~

Put~ \left($x, y\right) = \left($ℓn2, ℓn2\right)$

$- \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{α} +c . . . \left(2\right)$

Put \left($x, y\right) ≡ \left(0, - ℓn2\right)$~

$- 2 = $\dfrac{1}{α} +$c$

From equation \left(1\right) - \left(2\right),$~we get

\dfrac{{2}^{α} - 1}{α} = \dfrac{3}{2}

$⇒ \alpha = 2 ($ as $\alpha \in N )$.

questions.q: Let& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4y^{3} + 2yx^{2}}{3xy^{2} + x^{3}},$y\left(1\right) = 1$. If for some~$n \in N, y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$, then~$n& is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} \left(4y^{2} + 2x^{2}\right)\left(3y^{2} + x^{2}\right)$

Let~$y = vx$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$v + $x\dfrac{dv}{dx}

So,~\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} \left(4y^{2} + 2x^{2}\right)\left($3y^{2} + x^{2}\right)$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} =v \left($4v^{2} + 2\right)\left($3v^{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ $x\dfrac{dv}{dx} =$v \left( \left(4v^{2} + 2 - 3v^{2} - 1\right)3v^{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ ∫ \left(3v^{2} + 1\right)\dfrac{dv}{v^{3} + v} =$∫ $\dfrac{dx}{x}

$⇒ \ln \left|v^{3} + v\right| = \ln x + c$

$⇒ \ln \left|\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$3 + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| =$\ln x + c$

Given,~$y \left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ c = \ln 2$

So the equation becomes~$\ln \left| \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)3 + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| =$\ln x + \ln 2$

Now for~y\left($2\right)$

So putting~$x = 2$~in~\ln \left| \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$3 + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| =$\ln x + \ln 2$

~We get,~\ln \left(\dfrac{y3}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2}\right) =$2\ln 2 ⇒ $\dfrac{y3}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2} =$4$

$⇒ $\lleft[y\left(2\right)] = 2$

So,~$y\left(2\right) \in [ 2, 3 )$

So on comparing with~$y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$

$⇒ n = 3$

$

questions.q: Let $\alpha|x|=|y| \mathrme^{x y-\beta}, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{N}$ be the solution of the differential equation $x \mathrm{~d} y-y \mathrm{~d} x+x y(x \mathrm{~d} y+y \mathrm{~d} x)=0$, $y(1)=2$. Then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& a|x|=|y| e^{y x-\beta}, a, b \in N \\
& x d y-y d x+x y(x d y+y d x)=0 \\
& \frac{d y}{y}-\frac{d x}{x}+(x d y+y d x)=0 \\
& \ell n|y|-\ell n|x|+x y=c \\
& y(1)=2 \\
& \ell n|2|-0+2=c \\
& c=2+\ell n 2 \\
& \ell n|y|-\ell n|x|+x y=2+\ell n 2 \\
& \ell n|x|=\ell n\left|\frac{y}{2}\right|-2+x y \\
& |x|=\left|\frac{y}{2}\right| e^{x y-2} \\
& 2|x|=|y| e^{x y-2} \\
& \alpha=2 \quad \beta=2 \quad \alpha+\beta=4
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the tangent at any point $P$~on a curve passing through the points  \left(1, 1\right)$~and  \left(\dfrac{1}{10}, 100\right)$, intersect positive $x$-axis and $y$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively. If $PA: PB = 1: k$ and $y = y  \left(x\right)$~is the solution of the differential equation e\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$kx + $\dfrac{k}{2},$y\left(0\right) = k$, then $4y\left(1\right) - 5\log_{\mathrm{e}}3 is equal to _______________$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The tangent at any point $P$~on a curve passing through the points \left(1, 1\right)$~and \left(\dfrac{1}{10}, 100\right)$, intersect positive $x$-axis and $y$-axis at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively,

And $PA: PB = 1: k$ and $y = y \left(x\right)$~is the solution of the differential equation e\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$kx + $\dfrac{k}{2},$y\left(0\right) = k$,

Now on plotting the diagram we get,

Equation of tangent at $P \left(x, y\right)$ is :

$Y - y = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \left(X - x\right)$

Coordinate of~$A = \left(x - y\dfrac{dx}{dy},0\right)$

Coordinate of~$B = \left($0, y - $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)

$∴ \left($x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{kx - ky\dfrac{dx}{dy}}{k + 1}, \dfrac{y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{k + 1}\right)$

So,~$y = \dfrac{y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{k + 1}$

$⇒ y\left(k + 1\right) = y - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ ky = - x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ k\dfrac{dx}{x} = - \dfrac{dy}{y}$

Now integrating both side, we get

$kln | x | + ln | y | = lnC . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now given equation \left($i\right)$~passes through \left(1, 1\right)$ and~ \left(\dfrac{1}{10},$100\right)$

So,~$C = 1$ and~$k = 2$

Now putting the value of~$k$, we get

e\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$kx + $\dfrac{k}{2}

$⇒ $e\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$2x + 1 \left\{\text{as}k = 2\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} =\ln \left(2x + 1\right)$

Integrating the above equation we get,

$y = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(2x + 1\right) \left($\ln \left|2x + 1\right| - 1\right) + C$

And the above equation passes through~\left(0, 2\right)$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{5}{2}$

So,~$2y = \left(2x + 1\right)\lleft(\ln \left|2x + 1\right| - 1\right) + 5$

$⇒ 2y\left(1\right) = 3\left(\ln 3 - 1\right) + 5$

$⇒ 2y\left(1\right) = 3\ln \left(3\right) + 2$

Hence,~$4y\left(1\right) - 5\log_{\mathrm{e}}3 = 2\left[3\ln 3 + 2\right] - 5\ln 3$

$⇒ 4y\left(1\right) - 5\log_{\mathrm{e}}3 = 6\ln 3 + 4 - 5\ln 3$

$⇒ 4y\left(1\right) - 5\log_{\mathrm{e}}3 = 4 + \ln 3 \approx5$

Note: This question was bonus in Jee Mains 2023 April session.

$
